events.description: FRUITION’S FINAL TOUR As Fruition releases its eighth studio album, Something More, via Bloodshot Records, the acclaimed Americana band is also announcing plans to step away from touring following the scheduled tour dates, which now extend through January 2027. More than 15 years together, building a grassroots audience with stacked vocal harmonies and collaborative, song-driven Americana, this is American roots music at its broadest and boldest — a melting pot of rock, soul, folk, and pop. Produced by Grammy winner Tucker Martine (The Decemberists. My Morning Jacket), “...this album is the culmination of almost two decades of making music as Fruition,” explains Jay Cobb Anderson. Asked about the mission behind Something More, Kellen Asebroek shares: “We set out to show the world what we’ve learned along the way, both musically and personally, but perhaps more importantly, this album makes a point to be honest about the things we’ve had to UNLEARN. The truth of this album is found in kicking old habits, letting go of control, interrogating our motives, and approaching each session with fearless, open hearts.” Handmade Moments is a fearless, all-weather duo based in New Orleans, LA.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.description: Join us at Woodlawn this fall for our Historic Grounds series, where we bridge the gap between scholarly research and community dialogue. When : Third Saturday of the month, 2:00 pm – 3:30 pm Tickets: $35 (or book a Fall Pass and save 20%!) Join Francesco De Salvatore, the Director and Curator of the Alexandria Oral History Center, and descendants of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Cemetery (a historic African American burial ground) and the Colored Rosemont community (the site of some of the first African American homeowners in the City), as they discuss these two community history initiatives that are being completed in the City of Alexandria, VA. Itinerary: 2:00 pm : Join a subject matter expert for an in-depth exploration of local history and its national relevance. Engage in spirited conversation with the speaker over coffee and light refreshments. 3:00 pm : An exclusive experience tied to the day’s topic - such as a specialized tour or vault access to rarely seen collection objects. Your Ticket Includes: Lecture & Q&A: Admission to the keynote presentation and interactive Q&A session Vault Access: A viewing of rarely seen artifacts from the Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House Collection. Historic Tours: Access to the Woodlawn estate for open house tours. Refreshments: Complimentary coffee and light bites. About the speaker: Francesco De Salvatore is a public historian

events.title: Historic Grounds: Community History in Alexandria, VA, with Francesco De Salvatore
events.description: Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House presents Historic Grounds: Community History in Alexandria on Saturday, November 21st, 2026 from 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. at 9000 Richmond Highway in Alexandria, Fairfax County area, Virginia. This program is part of the Historic Grounds series, where scholarly research bridges with community dialogue. Each session pairs scholarly insight with discussion, offering a unique space to learn, reflect, and connect. Join Francesco De Salvatore, Director and Curator of the Alexandria Oral History Center, and descendants of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Cemetery (a historic African American burial ground) and the Colored Rosemont community (site of some of the first African American homeowners in Alexandria) as they discuss two community history initiatives being completed in Alexandria, Virginia. The afternoon unfolds as follows: 2:00 p.m. welcomes guests with subject matter expert exploration of local history and its national relevance, followed by spirited conversation over coffee and light refreshments. At 3:00 p.m., an exclusive experience tied to the day's topic offers specialized tours or vault access to rarely seen collection objects. Your ticket includes lecture and Q&A admission to the keynote presentation and interactive discussion; a copy of Freedom in the Age of Slavery: A History of Free People of Color in Virginia; vault access to rarely seen artifacts from the Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House Collection; access to the Woodlawn estate for open house tours; and complimentary coffee and light refreshments. Francesco De Salvatore is a public historian, memory worker, and archivist committed to ethical, stakeholder-driven historical preservation. They founded and direct the City of Alexandria's Alexandria Oral History Center, a community-driven collaboration documenting and preserving Alexandria's stories and memories. Francesco holds an M.A. in History from the University of Illinois at Chicago and an M.A. in American Studies from Geor

events.title: Indecent: The True Story of a Little Jewish Play
events.description: ASL Sign Interpreted Performance and Afterword discussion on Friday, November 20 . Written by Paula Vogel, Score and Original Music by Lisa Gutkin and Aaron Halva Directed by Sasha Olinick Performances will be held in the Theatre Arts Arena on the Montgomery College Rockville campus. In 1906 a young, up and coming Jewish/Polish writer, Sholem Asch, penned “God of Vengeance”, a play attacking religious hypocrisy and lovingly depicting a romantic relationship between two women. The play quickly became a hit as it toured throughout Europe and was translated from its original Yiddish into several different languages. But in America, when an English translation opened on Broadway in 1923, the play was quickly shut down and the cast, director and producer were jailed and prosecuted for violating obscenity laws. Indecent, by Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright Paula Vogel, charts the history of this incendiary drama and the path of the artists who risked their careers and lives to perform it. INDECENT is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Dramatists Play Service. Indecent is recommended for mature audiences and teenagers aged 13 and older due to adult themes and historical prejudice.

events.title: Jean Rondeau
events.description: Back by popular demand, the extraordinary Jean Rondeau returns to dazzle CMM audiences with his singular command of the harpsichord. Described by The Washington Post as “a master of his instrument with the sort of communicative gifts normally encountered in musicians twice his age,” Rondeau is the most exciting harpsichordist of his generation. His program celebrates the golden age of French Baroque keyboard music: Louis Couperin’s improvisatory grandeur, Rameau’s sparkling brilliance, François Couperin’s elegant wit, and Royer’s thrilling La Marche des Scythes. In the resonant sanctuary of First Lutheran Church, this music will transport you straight to Versailles.

events.description: 1pm • No Cover • $10-$20 suggested donation Jim Patton & Sherry Brokus Jim Patton and his wife and musical collaborator, percussionist Sherry Brokus , have a gift for turning everyday moments into songs with deeper meaning. Their new album, Pattonville, on Berkalin Records, turns that gift toward the past, gathering tales from years gone by, told from a deeply personal perspective. The album reached #2 on the Folk DJ Charts in June 2026, and Goldmine Magazine's Lee Zimmerman calls each song "a singular standout, brimming with feeling, finesse and an unmistakable emotional bond." Critic Geoffrey Himes praises "the distinctive body of work the duo has created over four decades."Following the full-band rock 'n' roll of Two True Loves, Pattonville trades some of that energy for reflection, finding in old stories the roots of the present and the common ground we all share.

events.title: Liana Flores
events.description: Liana Flores' story is one of cultural cross-pollination, unlikely chances, and quite possibly a signpost for the evolution of folk music in the digital age. Raised in rural Norfolk pre-internet ubiquity, the bossa nova CDs belonging to Liana's Brazilian mother were a first glimpse into a musical world beyond Eleanor Rigby on cassette and Gilbert & Sullivan in the village hall. At 19, she went from building an early listener base with showtune covers in the YouTube era, to penning her own songs. The influences all started coming together, in self-recorded songs combining the harmonic stylings of bossa nova guitar with personal lyrics - often gloomy but persevering, expressing anxieties and depicting the nature in her hometown. Three years later, one of these unassuming songs, ‘rises the moon’, was uploaded to TikTok without the singer's knowledge and became a surprise hit, spawning countless cover versions before the labels came calling. Nearly a billion streams later, it's arguably a defining folk song of its generation. After signing to Verve Records, a full-length record, Flower of the soul, followed in 2024. His first big break came in 1978 playing John Lennon in “Beatlemania”, first as an understudy in New York, then in the West Coast company, followed by a national touring company. Removing himself from that situation in Feb. 1980, Marshall settled in New York City. Enthralled by the hyper-diverse musical culture of the City, and the local Rock scene in particular, Marshall formed a Rock and Roll band with brother Robert on drums and Chris Donato on bass. Of his City Winery New York show last fall Infocus Visions Music & Arts Magazine hailed, “Marshall Crenshaw live is an experience in itself. Forget the solo artist; this is a full band explosion that showcases the magic of musical synergy. Watching them on stage is like peeking into a creative engine room. You see the interplay, the energy flowing between them, how each member feeds off the others to create that signature Marshall Crenshaw sound.”

events.description: Join Enough Adoption Foundation for a special children's book reading celebrating love, adoption, and the many ways families are formed. Enjoy an engaging story time followed by arts and crafts. Ideal for children ages 0–8. All families are welcome! Written by Mia Dickerson and her late mother, Margie Hampton, the story follows Mama Bear and Papa Bear as they prepare their home—and their hearts—for the arrival of their little girl, Mia. Through beautiful illustrations and gentle storytelling, children are introduced to adoption in a compassionate, age-appropriate way. As part of Enough's Adoption Literacy Program, this reading is more than story time. It's an opportunity to help children appreciate different family experiences, encourage kindness and understanding, and introduce language that helps adoptees feel seen, valued, and supported. Whether your family has been touched by adoption or you're simply looking to introduce your little one to the beauty of different families, all are welcome! Together, we're helping raise a generation of children who understand that families may be formed differently, but every child deserves to feel loved, worthy, and enough. Come read, learn, and celebrate belonging with us! Children must be accompanied by a parent or caregiver.

events.title: Miles Davis and John Coltrane Centennial
events.description: The year 2026 marks 100 years since the births of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, two visionaries of modern jazz. To mark the occasion, esteemed trumpeter and composer Terence Blanchard and saxophonist and composer Ravi Coltrane join forces for a centennial tribute celebrating the history, evolution, and continuing future of jazz. The two bandleaders bring distinct personal and artistic connections to this performance: Coltrane as the son of John Coltrane and Blanchard as one of today’s leading trumpeters, shaped by the music and innovation of Miles Davis. Together, they channel the creativity, freedom, and spirit of experimentation that defined Davis and Coltrane’s artistry. Rather than a nostalgic reenactment, the concert offers a reimagining grounded in the legacy of Davis and Coltrane while remaining anchored in the present. True to jazz’s essence, Blanchard, Coltrane, and their ensemble embrace improvisation, invention, and emotional intensity, allowing the music to evolve in the moment throughout the evening.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: South Lakes Theatre Arts Presents Come From Away
events.description: Come From Away, written by Irene Sankoff and David Hein, is a critically acclaimed musical featuring a poignantly relevant script and a deeply moving score. The show’s global presence resonates across all audiences as an uplifting reminder of humanity’s ability to come together, no matter what the circumstances. Based on real events of September 11th, 2001, Come From Away tells the story in which 38 planes, carrying thousands of passengers from across the globe, were diverted to the isolated community of Gander, Newfoundland. The locals of the small town played host to the world as they fed, housed, and comforted the stranded passengers for over four days. Inundated by culture clashes and language barriers, the people of Gander persevered, demonstrating the power of kindness. On the 10 th anniversary of 9/11 in 2011, Sankoff and Hein traveled to Gander to interview residents and returning passengers. They turned hundreds of distinct accounts into a celebrated musical. For this 25 th anniversary year of September 11th, South Lakes Theatre Arts is honored to bring these accounts to life. Content Warning: Some mature content & langage. Disclaimer: There will be NO intermission for this production.

Blanchard and Coltrane, both deeply connected to the spirit and lineage of these jazz icons, embody the very essence of creativity, futurism, transcendence, freedom—and the timeless “birth of cool” that defined Miles and Trane’s artistry. This centennial tribute will not be a nostalgic reenactment, but a bold reimagining. Each concert will be a living, breathing experience, rooted in the legacy of Davis and Coltrane, yet fully anchored in the now. True to jazz’s essence, the performances will embrace improvisation, invention, and emotional intensity, ensuring that every evening is unique and unrepeatable. A powerful celebration of heritage, transmission… and the future of jazz.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

He establishes an order built on using “might for right.” His ideals, however, are tested when his lovely queen, Guenevere, falls in love with his most loyal knight, Lancelot. Add in the dastardly Mordred and his wicked schemes and it soon appears this dream of a kingdom may only exist for one brief, shining moment. ​ This stirring Golden Age musical has enchanted generations of theatregoers with its sweeping score and iconic characters. It is a romance, a tragedy, a comedy, an adventure, a fantasy, and a stirring exploration of power and leadership all at once. And above all, it is a piece about the stories and ideals we pass along to future generations.​

events.title: Full Moon Gathering: Mindful Practices and Community Connection with Sabrina Remsburg
events.address: 30 W. Potomac St., Ste 102, Brunswick, MD 21716
events.description: This November Full Beaver Supermoon rises with a steady, grounding energy, symbolizing resilience, creation, and laying strong foundations for the future. Traditionally linked to a time of building and preparing for winter’s stillness, it reflects a period of securing what matters most and reinforcing both inner and outer stability. Spiritually, it encourages you to nurture your sense of home, protect your energy, and commit to the structures that support your growth. Beneath its luminous glow, we’re reminded to tend to what sustains us, release instability, and move forward with quiet strength and purpose. Our Full Moon Gatherings offer a supportive space to connect in community, move gently, and settle into meditation while clarifying intentions for the next lunar cycle. Through accessible practices such as Extra Gentle and Restorative Yoga, a deeply immersive sound bath, and other rituals, we honor the full moon as a time of release, clarity, and renewal - celebrating our own fullness while opening to the wisdom of what is yet to unfold. No previous yoga experience required.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Indecent: The True Story of a Little Jewish Play
events.description: ASL Sign Interpreted Performance and Afterword discussion on Friday, November 20 . Written by Paula Vogel, Score and Original Music by Lisa Gutkin and Aaron Halva Directed by Sasha Olinick Performances will be held in the Theatre Arts Arena on the Montgomery College Rockville campus. In 1906 a young, up and coming Jewish/Polish writer, Sholem Asch, penned “God of Vengeance”, a play attacking religious hypocrisy and lovingly depicting a romantic relationship between two women. The play quickly became a hit as it toured throughout Europe and was translated from its original Yiddish into several different languages. But in America, when an English translation opened on Broadway in 1923, the play was quickly shut down and the cast, director and producer were jailed and prosecuted for violating obscenity laws. Indecent, by Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright Paula Vogel, charts the history of this incendiary drama and the path of the artists who risked their careers and lives to perform it. INDECENT is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Dramatists Play Service. Indecent is recommended for mature audiences and teenagers aged 13 and older due to adult themes and historical prejudice.

Follow Jean-Valjean from his beginnings as convict #24601 to life in hiding, to protector of Cosette, pursued all the while by the relentless Javert, culminating in the revolutionary passions of the 1832 Paris uprising. Join us at the barricade this holiday season, and be stirred by a musical unmatched by its lyrical humor, its calls for justice, and its portrayal of the sacrifices one can make in the name of love. Featuring: Kevin S. McAllister as Javert, Alex De Bard as Eponine, Tracy Lynn Olivera as Madame Thénardier, Jordan Friend as Thénardier, Stephanie Waters as Fantine, Ben Clark as Marius, and more to be announced soon.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

The concert is sponsored by the St. Alban's Muldoon Concert fund and is free. events.title: The Lutheran Seminary in the Battle of Gettysburg
events.description: On July 1, 1863, the Civil War came to the Seminary's door, leaving in its wake countless stories of heroism and horror. The Lutheran Theological Seminary moved to the western side of Gettysburg in 1832, followed three decades later by national debates that tore apart the United States and divided the institution. As the Battle of Gettysburg opened on July 1, 1863, the Civil War came to the Seminary's door, leaving in its wake hundreds of wounded soldiers, thousands of dollars of property damage, and countless stories of heroism and horror. Explore the social, military, and medical impacts on this critical site through a brief history of its stories and legacies. Codie Eash serves as Director of Education and Interpretation at Seminary Ridge Museum and Education Center in Gettysburg, where he has served several roles as a member of the staff since 2012. In 2014, he earned a bachelor’s degree in communication/journalism from Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania, where he also completed a minor in History. In 2024, Codie began working on a master’s in American History at Gettysburg College through The Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History. In addition to Museum tours and programming, he lectures for American Battlefield Trust conferences, National Park Service sites, historical societies, Civil War roundtables, educational groups, and other organizations. Codie is a founding contributor to Pennsylvania in the Civil War , reviews books for Civil War Monitor and Emergin

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.description: There is no reason for GHOSTWOMAN’s fourth album to exist. Welcome to the Civilized World is born to a broken world; a corrupt inheritance – Evan Uschenko and Ille van Dessel are under no illusions about its futility – and yet, this thing is alive. It’s an allergic reaction to the times we are living in: a welt that screams to be itched, the purging of a modern sickness they could no longer stomach. Beyond rationality, this record came from a place of gut feeling and a lack of any other option. Hell may have cracked wide open – but GHOSTWOMAN will not go quietly. GHOSTWOMAN itself only exists because Uschenko and van Dessel were the ones “stupid enough to commit to it”. Conceived by Uschenko after cutting his teeth as a touring multi-instrumentalist, the project was brought to life in an abandoned farmhouse in Diamond City, Alberta. There, for two months, he would make the self-released, self-titled debut album which was produced and dubbed directly to custom-made cassette tapes. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.description: November 5-29, 2026 Step into the ring for The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity, a Pulitzer-Prize finalist comedy that body-slams the world of pro-wrestling, pop culture, and the performance of identity. Told through the eyes of Macedonio “The Mace” Guerra, a gifted wrestler stuck being paid to lose to a bigger-named star in the ring, this knockout satire takes on cultural stereotypes, media spectacle, and the courage it takes to say no. A bold, tour-de-force comedy that leaves it all on the mat! Audience Advisories: strong language, simulated violence/fighting, racial stereotypes, flashing lights and haze effects. The 2nd Sunday matinee of the run will be a mask required performance. Please bring a mask or one will be provided to you. Ticket Price: $45 Box Office: boxoffice@nextstoptheatre.org or (703) 481-5930 NextStop Theatre: 269 Sunset Park Driver, Herndon, VA 20170

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Cult of Love-Round House Theatre
events.description: Celebrate the holidays with the Broadway sensation Cult of Love ! In this gripping, music-filled play, four adult siblings (and their partners) return home for Christmas Eve, carrying secrets, resentments, and competing ideas of what family demands. As the singing and celebration give way to confrontation, old wounds reopen and new revelations emerge. Leslye Headland’s “stormy, compassionate, [and] cuttingly observant” ( TimeOut NY ) play interrogates the complexity of family loyalty, the power of religion, and what it truly means to love one another.

events.title: Swing 5 Jazz/ Includes beginner Balboa dance lesson @7:15
events.description: 7:15 Lesson 8:00pm Show • $10 - $20 Recommended Donation Swing 5 Swing 5 will transport you back to France in the 1930s. Begin with the heartbeat of a slap bass and the pulse of two rhythm guitars. Add to it melodic runs sweetly played on the accordion and a soaring fiddle. What you get is the Swing 5 band playing jazz and swing music from a time when a night out meant live music that provokes the uncontrollable urge to dance! Lead by talented local guitarist James Key and influenced by the legendary Django Reinhardt, this is a show you won't want to miss! YouTube • Live @Hank Dietle's Tavern Intro to Balboa Do you like listening to Swing 5 but find it challenging to dance to their energetic tempos? If so, come learn beginner Balboa with Tony Treston and Katherine Anderson! Experienced dance teachers Katherine and Tony, who regularly teach at Glen Echo, will be offering a free basic lesson in Balboa — a footwork-focused dance style which is tailor made for fast-tempo tunes and crowded dance floors — at 7:15 pm before Swing 5 takes the stage. Come for the 30-minute lesson, then stay to put your new moves into practice on the Hank Dietle’s dance floor! No partner needed.

events.description: Are you curious about the fascinating history behind Fort Washington? Whether you are a history buff or just looking to enjoy a scenic walk through the fort, this tour is perfect for all ages. Our knowledgeable guides will provide insights into the fort’s construction, its role in defense, and the stories of those who lived and served here. In the event of incliment weather (dangerous heat, thunderstorms, poor air quality, or freezing cold) this program will be moved inside the visitor center and abridge to 30 minutes. events.description: Modern classics don’t come any bigger than Les Misérables, and Olney Theatre celebrates it for the first time in honor of the show’s 40th anniversary. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: Join fellow book lovers for Literary Libations, a free monthly book club hosted in the Parlor Room at The Study at Morrison House. Taking place one Wednesday each month, this gathering offers a relaxed and welcoming space to dive into your next read—whether it's a timeless classic, a trending release, or the latest must-read from BookTok. Sip on themed cocktails and mocktails inspired by the book of the month, pair them with small plates from The Study's bar menu, or linger after the discussion to indulge in a seasonal tasting menu. Literary Libations isn't a formal, structured discussion—it's a cozy salon for mingling, exchanging ideas, and diving into new worlds together. Conversation starters and thoughtful prompts will be scattered around the room, but the conversation is all yours to shape. *SPECIAL DISCOUNT at Old Town Books when attendees mention Literary Libations at checkout! BOOK OF THE MONTH: The Night WatchmanBased on the extraordinary life of National Book Award-winning author Louise Erdrich's grandfather who worked as a night watchman and carried the fight against Native dispossession from rural North Dakota all the way to Washington, D.C., this powerful novel explores themes of love and death with lightness and gravity and unfolds with the elegant prose, sly humor, and depth of feeling of a master craftsman.Thomas Wazhashk is the night watchman at the jewel bearing plant, the first factory located near the Turtle Mountain Reservation in rural North Dakota. He is also a Chippewa Council member who is trying to understand the consequences of a new “emancipation” bill on its way to the floor of the United States Congress. It is 1953 and he and the other council members know the bill isn't about freedom; Congress is fed up with Indians. The bill is a “termination” that threatens the rights of Native Americans to their land and their very identity. How can the government abandon treaties made in good faith with Native Americans “for as long as the grasses shall grow, and the rivers run”?Since graduating high school, Pixie Paranteau has insisted that everyone call her Patrice. Unlike most of the girls on the reservation, Patrice, the class valedictorian, has no desire to wear herself down with a husband and kids. She makes jewel bearings at the plant, a job that barely pays her enough to support her mother and brother. Patrice's shameful alcoholic father returns home sporadically to terrorize his wife and children and bully her for money. But Patrice needs every penny to follow her beloved older sister, Vera, who moved to the big city of Minneapolis. Vera may have disappeared; she hasn't been in touch in months, and is rumored to have had a baby. Determined to find Vera and her child, Patrice makes a fateful trip to Minnesota that introduces her to unexpected forms of exploitation and violence, and endangers her life.Thomas and Patrice live in this impoverished reservation community along with young Chippewa boxer Wood Mountain and his mother Juggie Blue, her niece and Patrice's best friend Valentine, and Stack Barnes, the white high school math teacher and boxing coach who is hopelessly in love with Patrice.In the Night Watchman, Louise Erdrich creates a fictional world populated with memorable characters who are forced to grapple with the worst and best impulses of human nature. Illuminating the loves and lives, the desires and ambitions of these characters with compassion, wit, and intelligence, The Night Watchman is a majestic work of fiction from this revered cultural treasure.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Frosted at Franklin Park returns November 13, 2026 – January 9, 2027, turning Downtown DC’s largest green space into a sparkling winter wonderland. Enjoy the sparkling holiday lights while helping bring warmth to communities across the DMV, with a live radio broadcast from WPGC 95.5. events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.
